data.description:

Virtu Financial (VIRT)

Virtu Financial plugs into the screener theme as the picks and shovels behind modern trading, including crypto venues, using its market making and execution platforms to connect institutions to a wide range of assets.

Scaling invested trading capital from about US$2.0b a year ago to US$3.4b as of September 2026, supported by an incremental US$500m term loan and a medium term goal above US$4.0b, increases the capital base that can generate ANT and EBITDA.

Visa (V)

Visa links the crypto theme to everyday spending by running one of the largest global payment networks while experimenting with digital asset rails alongside its traditional card franchise.

Visa generates about US$46 billion from Payment Services and has a market value of roughly US$793 billion, which reflects the scale of its global payment network.

The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that Visa’s expanding role in digital money movement could matter far more than its limited direct crypto exposure today.

Continued build out of cross border and money movement solutions, including Visa Direct reaching 18 billion endpoints and about 12.5 billion to 12.6 billion transactions last year, together with scaled stablecoin settlement on nine blockchains, is broadening Visa's fee pools and can support net revenue and EPS growth.

What investors really have to weigh is how one pressure point on Visa’s future pricing power could reshape those earnings assumptions almost overnight.

That pricing hinge is exactly what full narrative for Visa unpacks. It reveals where Visa’s fee engine could stall, where it could accelerate, and which risks might be getting mispriced.

CoinShares (CSHR)

CoinShares builds crypto linked investment products and capital markets services, with Asset Management generating about US$107 million and Capital Markets around US$29 million, all from Jersey, on a market value of roughly US$473 million.

CoinShares gives you direct exposure to crypto capital markets through exchange like products, trading activity, and tokenization efforts, all in a single U.S. listed stock. data.title: The Bet Vertex Pharmaceuticals Holders Made
data.description:
If you only glanced at the headlines on Vertex Pharmaceuticals over the past year, the story might have looked muddled. Revenue pushed ahead while net margin in Q3 2026 dropped to 19.0% from 35.2% the year before, and investors fretted over a US$10b acquisition and gene therapy costs. Holding Vertex Pharmaceuticals over the past year would have returned 23.2%, including dividends. If you were weighing that decision a year ago, what did the early data really suggest about this mix of growth and pressure?

Vertex Pharmaceuticals has already moved. See which of 32 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On Vertex Pharmaceuticals

The shares cost US$435 at the start of the period, so you were effectively choosing between two very different stories about where Vertex Pharmaceuticals might head next.

On the optimistic side, one camp saw a Fair Value of US$480, a notional price based on assumptions that revenue could grow 9.4% a year and profit margin might reach 37.4% as gene editing and new therapies scaled.

The pessimistic view pointed to a Fair Value of US$330, a scenario where tighter drug pricing, high gene therapy costs, and heavy R&D spending risked compressing returns despite any pipeline progress.

What The Results Changed For Vertex Pharmaceuticals

The Crinetics deal and growing breadth of ALYFTREK, CASGEVY, Journavx and Palsonify supported parts of the optimistic Vertex Pharmaceuticals story around diversification and new franchises. The same period showed pressure on profitability as total revenue reached US$3,440.8m in Q3 2026 while net income was US$653.6m and net margin fell to 19.0%. The evidence pointed in both directions.

The central question here was not headlines about new therapies, but whether expanding into gene therapy and endocrinology could support margins. When you look at another drug developer, test the same claim directly against reported net income and margin rather than only watching top line progress or pipeline headlines.

What Today's Vertex Pharmaceuticals Price Already Assumes

Vertex Pharmaceuticals now trades at US$539, with this Narrative's Fair Value sitting below that level according to the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St. Over the past year, the share price gain of 23.2% leaves less room for forgiving missteps.

The Narrative argues that at this price, you need confidence that new pillars like CASGEVY, renal programs and Crinetics assets can scale into high margin franchises despite heavier spending. The key assumption a buyer must test is whether broader infrastructure and patient support costs can be absorbed while still lifting long term profitability.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Vertex Pharmaceuticals converts its expanded multi pillar portfolio, including CASGEVY, renal programs, acute pain, and endocrinology assets from Crinetics, into durable high margin franchises that justify the current premium attached to the stock. The numbers on guidance, acquisitions, and pipeline scale imply a share price that already bakes in successful diversification beyond cystic fibrosis and strong long term execution, leaving limited room for disappointment."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the lower Fair Value this Narrative argues for

Another Pillar Behind Drug Pipelines

One large healthcare group is leaning on a crowded pipeline instead. It is advancing treatments in cancer, heart health, respiratory care and infectious disease.

The strategy is not just adding products. Longer lasting regimens and more convenient dosing aim to keep patients on therapy.

This business is also using AI to refine drug discovery. That could reshape how many late stage projects it manages at once.

For Teekay, the big-picture belief is pretty simple. You need to think that tight tanker supply, healthy spot rates and disciplined capital allocation can keep turning a 34 vessel fleet and US$1.4b of cash into solid earnings, even as trade routes shift. The latest quarter of record operational results slots neatly into that story because it shows the fleet is actually capturing the pricing on offer rather than just talking about it.

data.description:
The recent earnings posted by DATA MODUL Aktiengesellschaft Produktion und Vertrieb von elektronischen Systemen (ETR:DAM) were solid, but the stock didn't move as much as we expected. However the statutory profit number doesn't tell the whole story, and we have found some factors which might be of concern to shareholders.

An Unusual Tax Situation

We can see that DATA MODUL Produktion und Vertrieb von elektronischen Systemen received a tax benefit of €1.3m. This is of course a bit out of the ordinary, given it is more common for companies to be paying tax than receiving tax benefits! The receipt of a tax benefit is obviously a good thing, on its own. And given that it lost money last year, it seems possible that the benefit is evidence that it now expects to find value in its past tax losses. However, our data indicates that tax benefits can temporarily boost statutory profit in the year it is booked, but subsequently profit may fall back. Assuming the tax benefit is not repeated every year, we could see its profitability drop noticeably, all else being equal. While we think it's good that the company has booked a tax benefit, it does mean that there's every chance the statutory profit will come in a lot higher than it would be if the income was adjusted for one-off factors.

Our Take On DATA MODUL Produktion und Vertrieb von elektronischen Systemen's Profit Performance

In its most recent report, DATA MODUL Produktion und Vertrieb von elektronischen Systemen disclosed a tax benefit, as we discussed above. Given that sort of benefit is not recurring, it's safe to say the statutory profit overstates its underlying profitability quite significantly. For this reason, we think that DATA MODUL Produktion und Vertrieb von elektronischen Systemen's statutory profits may be a bad guide to its underlying earnings power, and might give investors an overly positive impression of the company. The good news is that it earned a profit in the last twelve months, despite its previous loss. data.title: Rai Way S.p.A. (BIT:RWAY) Just Released Its Third-Quarter Earnings: Here's What Analysts Think
data.description:
Investors in Rai Way S.p.A. (BIT:RWAY) had a good week, as its shares rose 2.7% to close at €4.32 following the release of its third-quarter results. Results were roughly in line with estimates, with revenues of €72m and statutory earnings per share of €0.33. The analysts typically update their forecasts at each earnings report, and we can judge from their estimates whether their view of the company has changed or if there are any new concerns to be aware of. With this in mind, we've gathered the latest statutory forecasts to see what the analysts are expecting for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Following the latest results, Rai Way's six analysts are now forecasting revenues of €304.0m in 2027. This would be a modest 5.7% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of €304.0m and earnings per share (EPS) of €0.34 in 2027. So we can see that while the consensus made no real change to its revenue estimates, it also no longer provides an earnings per share estimate. This suggests that revenues are what the market is focusing on after the latest results.

View our latest analysis for Rai Way

There's been no real change to the consensus price target of €6.00, with Rai Way seemingly executing in line with expectations. The consensus price target is just an average of individual analyst targets, so - it could be handy to see how wide the range of underlying estimates is. There are some variant perceptions on Rai Way, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at €7.20 and the most bearish at €4.60 per share. These price targets show that analysts do have some differing views on the business, but the estimates do not vary enough to suggest to us that some are betting on wild success or utter failure.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. The period to the end of 2027 brings more of the same, according to the analysts, with revenue forecast to display 4.5% growth on an annualised basis. That is in line with its 4.8% annual growth over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to see their revenues grow 2.2% per year. So it's pretty clear that Rai Way is forecast to grow substantially faster than its industry.

The Bottom Line

The clear take away from these updates is that the analysts made no change to their revenue estimates for next year, with the business apparently performing in line with their models. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at €6.00, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.
